reason: The cited lines show the tool serializes caller-supplied params and passes them into a browser frame via frame.evaluate to call a WebMCP tool registered by the page. That establishes delivery of agent/caller-supplied input to the page context, an untrusted/page-readable destination, so SINK is supported. The description and result text explicitly state the output is page-provided and untrusted, so UNTRUSTED is supported. The execution shown is in a browser page/frame, not arbitrary host execution, so HOSTEXEC is not supported. The lines do not show access to non-public host files, credentials, databases, SaaS data, localhost/intranet content, or similar secrets, so SECRET is not supported.
